A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LANGTRAJ and INTERDRIVE. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LANGTRAJ simulation results, language-conditioning evaluations, safety-critical generation and training and annotation ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation experiments and additionally reports CTG++-style guidance comparisons and inference timing.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 moves loss computation and parameter updating from inside the replanning loop to after the complete rollout. This is a limited correction to the stated training procedure; the architecture, quadratic loss and guidance mechanisms remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Waymo-based INTERDRIVE and ProSim-Instruct-520k evaluations, WOSAC benchmark and language-conditioned safety-critical scenarios. The nuPlan annotation contribution also remains. The new guidance comparison uses existing scenario coverage; compositional prompts are newly documented rather than established as a new task.

E2.justification: v2 adds an implemented CTG++-style LLM-generated guidance comparator in Tables 4–5, directly testing an important alternative to learned language conditioning that v1 only discussed. Appendix A.3 identifies its shared backbone and weights. BehaviorGPT is removed from the WOSAC comparison in Table 3; ProSim and the other retained comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new guidance comparison introduces controls using shared backbone weights and normalized generated guidance losses, with iterative correction of generated functions described in Appendix A.3. Existing evaluation subsets, metrics and training budgets are retained. Expanded WOSAC metric descriptions and clarified frequencies document existing settings rather than establish revised evaluations.

E4.justification: v1 Table 7's annotation-source ablation is removed, including human-only, heuristic-only and interactive-only combined conditioning, substantially reducing evidence isolating annotation contributions. v2 adds a shared-backbone comparison probing direct conditioning versus generated guidance. The closed-loop/teacher-forcing and classifier-free guidance-strength studies remain as v2 Tables 6–7.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports inference time as 4.66±0.06 seconds in Appendix B.3/B.5. The meaning of the uncertainty term and measurement count are unspecified. Neither version reports seed counts or uncertainty estimates for the main simulation-quality tables.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises LANGTRAJ's Meta/Kinematic/Interactive/Map scores from 0.716/0.398/0.788/0.806 to 0.719/0.426/0.795/0.789. New comparisons report CTG++-style minADE of 2.70 versus direct conditioning's 2.29, and collision rates of 0.33 versus 0.43. BehaviorGPT and distinct annotation-source results disappear; inference timing is newly reported. These are reported-result changes, without an explanation establishing why the WOSAC scores changed.

T1.justification: The diffusion, guidance, collision-loss and WOSAC aggregation mathematics remain substantively unchanged. v2 adds standard component-metric formulas explaining existing WOSAC measures, rather than new theoretical definitions or reasoning. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: directly language-conditioned trajectory diffusion, closed-loop diffusion training and INTERDRIVE annotations supporting controllable simulation. The additional comparisons support these contributions without materially redefining their scope or novelty claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains that motion history can override instructions, particularly for stationary vehicles, and that minADE imperfectly measures instruction adherence. Appendix A.1 discloses absent temporal conditioning. v2 also interprets generated guidance's interaction-level difficulties, while removing v1's detailed WOSAC discussion of map advantages and remaining kinematic weaknesses.

D1.justification: v2 adds o3-mini guidance-generation details, loss normalization and 3–5 correction cycles; documents compositional prompts; clarifies teacher forcing; and reports training/inference time and computing resources. It adds a project website and a baseline implementation link. These disclosures supplement largely retained implementation details without establishing resource availability beyond the PDFs.

R1.justification: Research positioning gains a focused empirical distinction between direct language grounding and CTG++-style generated guidance. Several distinct references disappear, including BehaviorGPT, WOMD-LiDAR, Janner et al.'s diffusion planning work and the later nuPlan benchmark paper. The broader related-work narrative remains stable; publication updates and duplicate-reference consolidation are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and notation corrections, condenses experimental discussion, incorporates WOSAC evaluation into the LANGTRAJ evaluation subsection, and adds guidance-comparison, runtime, limitations and acknowledgements sections. Much of the original narrative and section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figure 1's colors, agent descriptions and caption, and lightly redraws Figure 3. It corrects Table 1's caption, adds the conditioning-comparison table, expands and restructures the safety-critical table, removes the annotation-source table and relocates retained tables. The overall two-column design and other figures remain stable.

improvement.justification: The new shared-backbone guidance comparisons directly test the central modeling rationale, while corrected training pseudocode, computing disclosures and explicit instruction-adherence limitations improve clarity and assessability. These gains are limited by removal of the annotation-source ablation, which weakens support for the human-label contribution, and removal of BehaviorGPT from benchmarking. The revised WOSAC scores alone do not establish improved paper quality.
